title: Customer Churn Prediction & Retention Analytics
summary: IBM Telco dataset (7,043 records) taken from raw data to a deployed real-time prediction app.
points: Took the IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset (7,043 records) from raw data to a deployed app: cleaning, preprocessing, training and evaluation.
Only 1,869 customers had churned versus 5,174 who stayed, so I compared four algorithms plus class-weighted versions. Logistic Regression came out best.
Lowered the classification threshold to 25% to catch more churners, and used model coefficients to find the main drivers: tenure, contract type and internet service.
Saved the pipeline with Pickle and built a Streamlit app for real-time predictions.

title: Heart Disease Risk Prediction (Explainable AI)
summary: Six algorithms compared; SHAP explains each patient's prediction in a Streamlit app.
points: Compared six algorithms: Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, SVM and KNN. Random Forest performed best.
On the held-out test set it reached 86.96% accuracy, 84.82% precision, 93.14% recall and 88.79% F1. Five-fold cross-validation averaged 81.39% accuracy.
Used SHAP to show how each feature affected an individual patient's prediction, and built a Streamlit app so non-technical users can read the results easily.

title: California Housing Price Prediction
summary: Regression pipeline on California census data with live price predictions.
points: Built a regression pipeline on California census data and compared Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest regressors. Tuned the Random Forest (n_estimators=200, min_samples_leaf=2).
Test results: R² 0.818, MAE 0.273, RMSE 0.423. Median income and location were the strongest predictors.
Saved the model with Pickle and deployed a Streamlit app for live price predictions.

title: NLP Text Analysis Using TF-IDF
summary: A text processing pipeline that transforms raw text into meaningful numerical features using NLP techniques and TF-IDF.
points: Built a text preprocessing workflow to prepare raw text for analysis and machine learning.
Applied lowercase conversion, punctuation cleaning, tokenization and stop word removal where appropriate.
Used TF-IDF vectorization to transform cleaned text into numerical features based on word importance.
Organized preprocessing steps into a consistent workflow to avoid repeating unnecessary transformations.
Explored how numerical text representations can support NLP tasks such as text classification and similarity analysis.
